findings: Both captures present the same four pricing models. Businesses define products or services as Products and set amount, currency and billing cadence through Prices, while customers select service tiers, buy per-user units, or are charged under the documented quantity- or usage-based models. The overview supplies design patterns and links beyond the page. It contains no API sequence, eligibility gate or subscription lifecycle transition (old 6–21, new 7–22).

The usage-based row describes unchanged model options and now points to the Billing usage-based overview (old 15, new 16). Its separately captured November destination introduces Metronome and links to Stripe integration, architecture and migration guidance. That is evidence of the destination’s content and the changed route, not a new Metronome prerequisite or removal of a Stripe usage-based model in this overview.

The current source (lines 13–27) accurately summarizes the four model families and routes to the more detailed design source. The subscription concept's design paragraph and source list (lines 12 and 228–234) preserve the model distinctions and provide the reciprocal route.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the 2026-05-12 raw as dated historical authority for the same four descriptive models and the former usage-based link. Keep the separate usage-based implementation source and subscription design guide scoped to their own captured content.
unresolved_questions: The retargeted link does not establish redirects, availability or retirement of the May linked implementation guide. The source and its separately captured November destination do not provide universal migration requirements, entitlement, charge or invoice lifecycle behavior.

findings: Source lines 13–27 capture the unchanged four model descriptions. Its related pages already point to the subscriptions concept and integration design source.
source_assessments.reason: A dated raw reference can preserve the usage-based link change. The model semantics and existing source summary need no factual correction.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/pricing-models, old raw lines 6-21 and new raw lines 7-22 describe how businesses combine Products for what they sell with Prices for how much and how often to charge, including currency and recurring service period. The four examples are a customer choosing a flat-rate service tier, per-user or license units, tiered unit prices that vary with quantity or usage, and usage-based charging via fixed fee with overage, pay as you go or credit burndown. Both captures supply pricing design choices and links without documenting a state transition, setup workflow or eligibility test. The existing source-stripe-recurring-pricing-models.md covers all four patterns and points to the subscriptions concept and integration design source.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/pricing-models, old raw lines 6-21 and new raw lines 7-22 preserve the same pricing model behavior. The shorter table delimiter is formatting, and the Usage-based link changes from the subscriptions pricing model guide in May to the Billing usage-based overview in November, with the other three model links and See also routes retained. The linked November overview presents Metronome and migration resources using its own dated evidence. This routing change establishes no universal migration or Metronome requirement, retirement of the May destination or model removal. Retain the May provenance and original link history, record the November raw as a reference, and preserve the provider index and reciprocal wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md route for source-stripe-recurring-pricing-models.md. Its design guide link provides separate detail and no model conflict requires a factual correction.
